note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: The workshop manager asks an inspector to pass a frame that is 6 mm out of tolerance, "just this once". What should the inspector do?
options: Record a non-conformance and refer it for a decision
Pass it, as the manager is senior to the inspector on site
Pass it, but tell the welder to take more care next time
Change the tolerance on the drawing so that the frame passes

questions.stem: Before inspecting a fabricated job, which documents does the inspector need?
options: The welders' pay slips and the time sheets for the job
The steel supplier's price list and its delivery notes
The drawings, specification, code limits and ITP
The paint colour chart and the client's site address

questions.stem: Why does an inspector shine a torch at a low angle across a weld surface?
options: It warms the weld so that cracks open up wider
The shadows show up undercut, ripples and cracks
It dries the surface so the paint will stick to it
It shows the true colour of the heat tint on the toe

questions.stem: Which gauge can measure undercut depth, cap height, misalignment and bevel angle?
options: A fillet gauge, which reads leg length only
A feeler gauge, which reads small gaps only
A radius gauge, which reads the toe shape only
A multi-purpose (bridge cam type) weld gauge

questions.stem: For this job, the limit is a total pore diameter of 10 mm in any 100 mm of weld. In one 100 mm length you find pores of 2, 3, 1.5 and 4 mm. What is the result?
options: Accept: no single pore is larger than 4 mm
Accept: the total is exactly at the limit
Reject: the total of 10.5 mm is over the limit
Reject: any porosity at all fails the weld

questions.stem: How does dye penetrant testing show a crack?
options: Dye drawn into the crack bleeds out into the developer
The developer turns red wherever the steel is too hard
The crack glows when a magnet is held against it
The dye fills the crack and makes it stronger

questions.stem: Why must the surface be cleaned and dried before the penetrant is put on?
options: So the developer dries faster once it is sprayed
So the red dye matches the colour of the steel
So the inspector's gloves do not get stained
Dirt or water in a crack stops the dye getting in

questions.stem: When the excess penetrant is removed, why is the cleaner put on a cloth and not sprayed straight onto the weld?
options: Spraying uses up the can of cleaner far too quickly
Spraying can wash the dye out of the defects as well
The cleaner turns the developer pink if it is sprayed
Spraying leaves streaks that look like real cracks

questions.stem: Why must the penetrant be left on for the dwell time the maker gives?
options: So the penetrant dries hard and can be peeled off
So the steel cools down enough to touch safely
So it has time to seep into fine defects
So the colour of the dye can fade a little

questions.stem: A steel part has been lying in the sun and is too hot to touch. What should be done before dye penetrant testing?
options: Let it cool into the temperature range the maker gives
Test it at once, since the heat makes the dye work much faster
Cool it quickly with water from a hose, then test it
Use twice the amount of penetrant to make up for it

questions.stem: Why can magnetic particle testing not be used on austenitic stainless steel welds?
options: The particles stick too hard to stainless steel
Stainless steel welds never have any cracks
The contrast paint will not dry on stainless
The steel is not magnetic, so no field forms

questions.stem: Why is magnetic particle testing done twice on each area, with the yoke turned about 90° the second time?
options: The first test always magnetises the part too weakly
A crack that lies along the field does not show up
Turning the yoke cleans the ink off the surface
The code asks for two tests to save time later

questions.stem: What is a yoke lift test used for?
options: To check the yoke is strong enough before testing
To find out how heavy the part being tested is
To check the inspector can lift the yoke safely
To lift small parts off the bench after testing

questions.stem: Why is a thin white contrast paint sprayed on before black magnetic ink is used?
options: To stop the weld from rusting after the test
To magnetise the steel before the yoke is used
So the black indications show up clearly
So the client can see where the test was done

questions.stem: Which flaws can magnetic particle testing find?
options: Porosity deep in the middle of a thick weld
Lack of root fusion in 50 mm thick plate
The hardness of the heat-affected zone
Cracks at or just below the surface

questions.stem: Why is a gel or oil (couplant) used between the ultrasonic probe and the steel?
options: To stop the probe scratching the paint on the steel
Sound will not pass across an air gap into the steel
To keep the probe cool while it is being used
To clean the surface as the probe is moved along

questions.stem: What is a main advantage of ultrasonic testing over radiography on thick butt welds?
options: It gives a picture on film to keep for many years
It can be done by anyone without any training
No radiation, and it can find how deep a flaw is
It needs no cleaning of the surface at all

questions.stem: On a weld radiograph, what is the image quality indicator (IQI) used for?
options: To show the image is sharp enough to see small flaws
To mark the welder's number on the film
To measure the thickness of the cap on the weld
To show which way up the film was placed

questions.stem: On a radiograph, a straight dark line runs along the centre of the root. What does this usually show?
options: Excess cap height
A tungsten inclusion
Spatter on the plate
Lack of root penetration

questions.stem: Round dark spots scattered through the weld image on a radiograph usually show what?
options: Tungsten inclusions
Porosity
Excess penetration
Arc strikes

questions.stem: A small bright white spot shows on the radiograph of a TIG weld. What is it most likely to be?
options: A gas pore
A tungsten inclusion
A crater crack
A burn-through

questions.stem: A fillet-welded carbon steel bracket must be checked on site for surface cracks. Which of these tests suits best?
options: Radiography
Ultrasonic testing
Hardness testing
Magnetic particle testing

questions.stem: What does a fillet weld break test show?
options: Root fusion, and any porosity or slag inside the fillet
The tensile strength of the plate in megapascals
The hardness of the cap at each toe of the weld
The amount of distortion caused by the welding

questions.stem: When preparing a macro section, why is the cut face filed and sanded smooth before it is etched?
options: So the section weighs the same as a standard one
So the etchant can be wiped off more easily
Scratches would hide the outline of the weld
So the section can be welded back on later

questions.stem: In a macro section of a fillet weld, the weld metal has not reached the root corner of the joint. What is this called?
options: Incomplete root penetration
Excess convexity
Undercut at the toe
Overlap

questions.stem: In a nick-break test on a butt weld, why are saw cuts made into the weld first?
options: To let the welder see his passes before the break
To make the specimen fit inside the bending jig
To remove the cap so the weld is the right height
So that the break runs through the weld metal

questions.stem: What is camber on a fabricated beam?
options: A twist of the beam about its long axis
An upward or downward bow along its length
A sideways bow along its length, seen from above
An end plate that is not square to the beam

questions.stem: Seen from above, a welded beam bows sideways along its length. What is this called?
options: Camber
Twist
Sweep
Skew

questions.stem: For this job, the specification allows camber of up to the length ÷ 1000. What is the most allowed on an 8 m beam?
options: 0.8 mm
80 mm
8 mm

questions.stem: How can twist in a long welded frame be checked?
options: Sight across two straight edges laid on the ends
Measure its weight on a scale at each end
Tap it with a hammer and listen to the sound
Measure the length of each side with a tape

questions.stem: How is the flatness of a welded base plate checked?
options: By looking along it from one corner
By pouring water on it to see where it runs
With a straight edge in several directions, and feelers
By measuring its thickness with calipers at each of the four corners

questions.stem: On a connection plate, the bolt hole pitch is drawn as 70 mm ± 1 mm. You measure 71.5 mm centre to centre. What is the result?
options: Within tolerance, as it is only 1.5 mm out
Out of tolerance: record it as a non-conformance
Within tolerance, as holes can be reamed on site
Out of tolerance, so drill a new hole beside it

questions.stem: When inspecting a bolted steel connection, how far should the bolt normally stand out past the nut?
options: At least flush with the nut, often by a thread or more
It must stop at least two threads short of the nut face
Exactly 50 mm past the nut on every size of bolt
It does not matter, as long as the nut is tight

questions.stem: A joint uses tension-indicating washers with small bumps. What does the inspector check?
options: That the washers are painted the same colour as the steel
That the bumps still stand up fully under the nut
That each washer has been fitted upside down
That the bumps have closed as the maker's instructions say

questions.stem: Why must a weld be inspected and released before it is painted?
options: Paint will not stick to a weld that has not been passed
The painter needs the weld map to know the colour
Paint can hide cracks and other surface faults
A painted weld is too hot to inspect afterwards

questions.stem: An inspector is to witness a welder's qualification test but arrives after the root has been run. What should he do?
options: Accept the root, as the welder says it went well
Ask for the test to be restarted in his presence
Accept the test if the cap looks good to him
Let another welder sign that the root was seen

questions.stem: Which is the best way to show where a defect is on an inspection report?
options: Write "near the middle" beside the weld number
Describe it from memory at the end of the week
Tell the welder where it is and leave it off the report
A sketch with the weld number, a datum and the distance

questions.stem: Before inspecting welds high up on a steel frame, what must the inspector check?
options: That the access is safe, with fall protection if needed
That the welds are still hot enough for any cracks to show up clearly
That the welders have gone home for the day
That the paint on the frame is fully dry

questions.stem: How should cloths soaked in penetrant and cleaner be dealt with after testing?
options: Leave them on the bench to dry out in the sun
Burn them in the scrap bin at the end of the day
Put them in a closed metal bin away from heat
Wash them in the hand basin for the next test

questions.stem: A magnetic particle yoke runs on mains power. Which check comes first before using it?
options: That the ink can is full and well shaken up
That its lead, plug and case are undamaged and tested
That the contrast paint matches the yoke's colour
That the part has been painted with primer

questions.stem: What is an inspection release note (or certificate of conformity) for?
options: To record that the item passed and may go on
To show the price of the inspection to the client
To list the welders who should be paid a bonus
To order more steel for the next part of the job

questions.stem: A butt joint in 12 mm plate has a 2 mm step between the plate faces. For this job the limit is 10% of the thickness. What is the result?
options: Accept: it is under 3 mm
Accept: it is exactly 10%
Accept: steps do not matter
Reject: it is over 1.2 mm

questions.stem: On a concave fillet weld, why does the inspector check the throat as well as the legs?
options: The legs of a concave fillet are always undersized
The throat shows how fast the welder travelled
A concave face can leave the throat too thin
The legs cannot be measured on concave welds

questions.stem: On a full-penetration tee joint, which fit-up check matters most before welding starts?
options: That the plates have been painted with primer
Root gap and bevel, so the root can fully fuse
That the tacks are as large as the final weld
That the joint is set up in the overhead position

questions.stem: At final inspection, you find a weld that was painted before anyone inspected it. What is the right action?
options: Pass it, as the paint looks even and well applied
Pass it, if the welder signs that it was good
Remove the paint there, inspect the weld and record it
Reject the whole item and send it for scrap

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the thin white coating sprayed on after the excess penetrant is removed, to draw the dye out of defects?
What is the name of the time the penetrant is left on the surface before the excess is removed?
What is the name of the hand-held part of an ultrasonic set that sends sound into the steel and picks up the echoes?
Each weld radiograph must show an IQI. What do these letters stand for?
What is the name of the hand-held electromagnet with two legs, placed either side of a weld for magnetic particle testing?
On an etched macro section, what is the name of the boundary where the weld metal meets the parent metal?
What is the name of the distance from the centre of a bolt hole to the nearest edge of the plate?
What is the name of the test in which a fillet weld is broken by bending the upright plate over, so the fracture face can be examined?
What is the name of a cut cross-section of a weld that is polished and etched so its fusion and passes can be seen?
What two-letter abbreviation is used for dye (liquid) penetrant testing on an inspection report?
In NDT, what name is given to any sign seen, such as a line of magnetic particles, before it has been judged to be a defect or not?
An NDT company's report lists UT against each column splice weld. What do these letters stand for?
A frame is drawn 2400 mm long, and the specification allows ± 3 mm. What is the shortest length that passes, in mm?
What is the name for removing the magnetism left in a part after magnetic particle testing, where the specification asks for it?
What is the name of the steel block, with known holes or notches, used to set up an ultrasonic flaw detector before testing?

essays.stem: Choose a test method for each of these jobs and explain your choice: (a) surface cracks in fillet welds on a carbon steel crane bracket; (b) cracks in a stainless steel food tank weld; (c) buried lack of fusion in a 25 mm butt weld in a building column; (d) a lasting record of a pipe butt weld for the client's file.
essays.modelAnswer: (a) Magnetic particle testing suits the carbon steel bracket. The steel is magnetic, the test is quick on site, and it finds cracks at or just below the surface, which is where fatigue cracks start on fillet toes. (b) Stainless steel used for food tanks is usually not magnetic, so magnetic particle testing will not work. Dye penetrant testing finds cracks open to the surface on any non-porous metal, so it is the right choice. (c) Lack of fusion buried in thick plate cannot be seen by surface methods. Ultrasonic testing is best for a thick butt weld in a column: it finds planar flaws such as lack of fusion well, gives their depth and length, and needs no radiation barrier on a busy site. (d) Radiography gives a film or digital image of the whole weld that can be kept in the client's file and looked at again later. It needs licensed operators and a cleared area. In every case the test is done by a qualified operator to a written procedure.
markingPoints: (a) MT, with reasons: magnetic steel, surface cracks, quick
(b) PT, because stainless is not magnetic
(c) UT, for buried planar flaws in thick plate, gives depth, no radiation
(d) RT, for a lasting image record; licensed operators and cleared area
Tests done by qualified operators to a procedure

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would carry out a colour-contrast dye penetrant test on a weld, and how you would record the result.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the part is within the temperature range the maker gives and read the SDS. I remove slag, spatter and paint, then clean the weld and a band each side with the cleaner and let it dry, so nothing blocks the defects. I apply the penetrant over the area and leave it for the dwell time the maker gives, keeping it wet. I remove the excess by wiping with a dry cloth, then with a cloth damped with cleaner, never spraying cleaner straight on the weld, so dye is not washed out of defects. I shake the developer and spray a thin, even coat from the distance the maker gives. After the development time I inspect under good light. Red lines show cracks or lack of fusion; red dots show pores. I measure each indication and judge it against the code limits. I record the weld number, products and batch numbers, times, a sketch of indications, the result and my name, then clean the part.
markingPoints: Temperature check, safety (SDS), pre-cleaning and drying
Penetrant applied and left for the maker's dwell time
Excess removed with a cloth, not by spraying cleaner directly
Thin even developer, development time, inspection in good light; indications measured and judged
Record: weld, products, times, sketch, result, name; post-clean

essays.stem: Describe how you would carry out magnetic particle testing on a fillet weld with an AC yoke, white contrast paint and black ink, including the checks you would make on the equipment.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the yoke's lead, plug and case are undamaged and in test, and do a lift test with the test weight to show it is strong enough. I check the ink is mixed and do a quick check on a test piece with a known flaw, if one is available. The weld is cleaned of slag and spatter, then a thin, even coat of white contrast paint is sprayed and allowed to dry. I place the yoke legs either side of the weld, switch on, and apply the ink while the field is on, then let the ink drain before switching off. Particles gather at cracks lying across the field. I then turn the yoke about 90° and test the same area again, because a crack running along the field will not show. I move along the weld with the tested areas overlapping. Each indication is measured and judged against the code limits. I record the weld, equipment, results with a sketch, and my name, and clean off the ink and paint.
markingPoints: Equipment checks: electrical condition and lift test
Surface cleaned and contrast paint applied
Yoke placed across the weld, ink applied with the field on
Second test at about 90°, with overlapping areas
Indications measured, judged and recorded; part cleaned

essays.stem: Explain how a weld radiograph and its report are read: the checks on image quality and the appearance of the common weld flaws. Say what the welding inspector's part is, if he is not a qualified radiographic interpreter.
essays.modelAnswer: First the image is checked for quality: the image quality indicator must show the wire or hole size the procedure asks for, the density must be in range, and the markers must show the weld number and location so the image can be matched to the weld. Then the weld is read. Gas pores show as round dark spots. Slag inclusions show as dark, uneven shapes or lines. Lack of root penetration shows as a straight dark line along the centre of the root. Lack of side fusion shows as a dark line along the edge of the weld. Cracks show as fine, dark, wavy lines. Tungsten inclusions show as bright white spots, because tungsten is denser than steel. The images must be read and signed by a qualified interpreter. If the welding inspector is not qualified, he checks the report covers every weld on the weld map, records the results and repairs, and raises any query with the testing company.
markingPoints: Image quality: IQI, density, markers matched to the weld
Porosity and slag appearance
Lack of penetration and lack of fusion appearance
Cracks and tungsten inclusions appearance
Interpretation by a qualified person; inspector checks coverage, records results and raises queries

essays.stem: Describe how you would carry out the dimensional inspection of a fabricated steel beam, about 8 m long, with end plates and bolt holes, before it is released.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the tape and tools are in calibration and read the drawing and the tolerances in the specification. I set the beam on level supports so it does not sag. I measure the overall length between end plate faces and the section depth and flange width at each end and the middle. I check camber by stretching a fine line, or using a level, along the top flange and measuring the largest gap, and check sweep the same way along the side of a flange. I check twist by sighting across straight edges laid on the two ends. I check that the end plates are square to the beam and flat, using a square and a straight edge with feelers. I measure the bolt hole pitch, gauge, edge distances and hole sizes from a stated datum. Every reading is written on the inspection sheet against its tolerance. Anything out of tolerance is marked and raised as a non-conformance; if all pass, I sign the release.
markingPoints: Calibrated tools, drawing and tolerances; beam set level on supports
Length, depth and width measured at stated points
Camber, sweep and twist checked by line, level or straight edges
End plates: square and flat; holes: pitch, gauge, edge distance, size from a datum
Readings recorded against tolerances; NCR or release

essays.stem: Describe how a macro section and a fillet weld break test are prepared and judged.
essays.modelAnswer: For a macro section, a slice is sawn across the weld at a place set by the test rules, away from the start and stop. The cut face is filed and then sanded with finer and finer paper until it is smooth, with no deep scratches. It is etched with the etchant the Centre approves, using gloves, goggles and ventilation as the SDS says, then rinsed and dried. The etch shows the weld metal, the passes, the heat-affected zone and the fusion line. The inspector checks root fusion and penetration, fusion to both plates, leg lengths and throat, and looks for cracks, porosity, slag and lack of fusion against the code limits. For a fillet break test, a length of fillet weld is broken by bending the upright plate over towards the weld, in a press or with a hammer, so the weld root opens. The fracture face is checked for root fusion, porosity and slag, and judged against the limits. Both results are recorded with photos.
markingPoints: Macro: sawn at the right place, filed and sanded smooth
Etched safely as the SDS says; shows fusion, passes and HAZ
Macro judged: penetration, fusion, size, internal flaws against limits
Fillet break: how it is broken so the root opens
Fracture face judged; results recorded with photos

essays.stem: Describe how you would inspect a bolted steel connection on a fabricated frame, from the bolts and holes to the final tightness.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the drawing and specification for the bolt grade, size, length and tightening method. I check the bolts, nuts and washers are the right grade by their head and nut markings, and that they are clean and not damaged. I check the holes are the right size, in the right place, not torn or burred, and have not been enlarged by flame cutting. The plates must sit tight together, with no gaps beyond the limit, and contact faces must be as the specification says, for example unpainted where friction grip is needed. Washers must be under the part that is turned, and the right way up. Each bolt should stand out at least flush with the nut, usually by a thread or more. I then check tightness by the method given: snug tight, a marked turn of the nut, a torque check, or tension-indicating washers checked as the maker says. Each connection is recorded on the inspection sheet.
markingPoints: Checks bolt grade, size and length against the drawing, by markings
Hole size, position and condition; no flame-enlarged holes
Plates tight together; contact faces as specified; washers placed correctly
Bolt stand-out past the nut
Tightness checked by the specified method; recorded

essays.stem: Explain how an inspector should deal with a non-conforming item, the choices for what happens to it, and how the inspector stays independent when under pressure to pass work.
essays.modelAnswer: When an item does not meet the drawing, specification or code, the inspector marks it, puts it in a quarantine area or tags it so it cannot be used by mistake, and writes a non-conformance report giving the item, the requirement, what was found, with measurements and a sketch or photo. The choices for the item, called the disposition, are: rework to meet the drawing, repair to an approved procedure, use as it is with a written concession from the customer or engineer, regrade for another use, or scrap. The inspector does not decide a concession alone; the authorised person does, in writing. After rework or repair, the item is inspected again. To stay independent, the inspector judges only against the written limits, records the facts honestly, never signs for work he has not seen, and refers any pressure from managers, welders or the client to the person named in the quality system. His signature must always mean the work truly passed.
markingPoints: Mark and quarantine the item; write an NCR with facts
Lists disposition choices: rework, repair, use as is, regrade, scrap
Concession only in writing by the authorised person
Re-inspection after rework or repair
Independence: judge against written limits, honest records, refer pressure, never sign unseen work

essays.stem: Explain what makes a good weld and fabrication inspection report, and describe what it should contain.
essays.modelAnswer: A good report lets someone who was not there understand exactly what was inspected, how, and what was found. It should give the job, drawing number and revision, item and weld numbers from the weld map, the material and process, and the code or specification with the acceptance limits used. It should state the inspection method and stage, the equipment used with its calibration or serial numbers, the conditions, and the date. Results are given for each weld or dimension, with measurements, not just "good" or "bad". Each defect is described by type and size, with its position shown on a sketch from a datum, and photos where useful. The report says accept or reject against each limit, lists any non-conformance report raised, and is signed and dated by the inspector with their qualification. It should be clear, legible and written in plain words, so that repairs can be found and done, and filed so it can be traced later.
markingPoints: Identifies job, drawing revision, item and weld numbers, code and limits
States method, stage, equipment and calibration, date
Measured results for each weld or dimension
Defects described and located on a sketch or photo; accept or reject; NCRs listed
Signed, clear and filed for traceability

essays.stem: Explain how an inspector checks, from the records, that the welding on a job was done by qualified welders to approved procedures with the right materials.
essays.modelAnswer: The inspector starts from the weld map, which lists every weld with its welder and WPS. For each WPS, he checks it is approved and is backed by a procedure qualification record whose ranges cover the joint, material, thickness, position and consumables used. For each welder, he checks the qualification record covers the process, position and thickness of the welds that welder made, that it was signed by the examiner, and that the continuity record shows it was still current on the dates the welds were made. He checks the mill certificates against the heat numbers marked on the steel and recorded on the job, so the material is the grade the drawing calls for. He checks consumable certificates and the issue and oven logs, and the preheat and NDT records where needed. Any gap, such as a welder without a valid qualification for a weld, is raised as a non-conformance and the weld is reviewed or retested.
markingPoints: Uses the weld map to link welds, welders and WPSs
WPS approved and covered by a PQR
Welder qualification covers the work and was current (continuity)
Material traceability: heat numbers matched to mill certificates; consumable records
Gaps raised as non-conformances and welds reviewed or retested

practical1.title: Dye penetrant and magnetic particle testing of welded test pieces, with an inspection report
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a set of welded test pieces (carbon steel fillet and butt welds, and one stainless steel weld if the Centre has one), some with known or planted surface flaws, and the acceptance limits for the job. As a group, first plan the work: which test suits each piece and why, the order of work, and who does each step. Then carry out a colour-contrast dye penetrant test on at least two pieces and a magnetic particle test with a yoke, contrast paint and black ink on at least two carbon steel pieces, following the maker's instructions. Every member carries out at least one step of each test (cleaning, applying, removing, developing, magnetising, reading) and judges at least one indication. Measure each indication, mark it on a sketch, judge it against the limits and write an inspection report for each piece. Photograph each stage.
materials: Welded test pieces with known or planted flaws, and acceptance limits (from the assessor)
Colour-contrast dye penetrant kit: cleaner, penetrant, developer, lint-free cloths
AC magnetic yoke with lift test weight, white contrast paint and black magnetic ink
Steel rule, magnifier, torch, timer and marker
Inspection report forms and sketch sheets
Safety data sheets for all the sprays
photos: The group's test plan, showing the test chosen for each piece
A piece being pre-cleaned for dye penetrant testing
Developer on a piece, with indications showing
The yoke lift test being done
Indications on a magnetic particle test, in both yoke directions
The completed inspection reports with sketches
checklist: Chose a suitable test for each piece and gave a sound reason
Cleaned the surface properly before testing
Kept to the maker's dwell and development times
Removed excess penetrant with a cloth, without spraying cleaner directly
Checked the yoke and tested in two directions about 90° apart
Measured and judged indications correctly against the limits
Wrote a clear report with a sketch, result and signature
safety: Read the SDS; use the sprays only in a well-ventilated area, away from heat and flames
Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses
Check the yoke's lead and plug before use; keep it away from water
Put used cloths in a closed metal bin

practical2.title: Dimensional and bolted-connection inspection of a fabricated beam or frame, ending in a release note or NCR
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a fabricated steel beam or frame with welded end plates and at least one bolted connection, its drawing, and the tolerances for the job. Some errors may have been built in. As a group, plan the inspection: the checks, the tools, the datums, the order and who does what. Set the item level on supports. Then measure and record: overall length, section sizes at stated points, camber and sweep with a fine line or level, twist with straight edges, end plate squareness and flatness, and bolt hole pitch, gauge, edge distances and sizes. Inspect the bolted connection: bolt grade markings, washers, stand-out past the nut and the tightening method. Visually inspect the welds. Each member is responsible for one group of checks and checks another member's readings. Compare every reading with its tolerance, then write either a signed release note or a non-conformance report for each fault, with a sketch. Photograph each stage.
materials: Fabricated beam or frame with end plates and a bolted connection (from the assessor)
Drawing and the tolerances for the job
Steel tape and rule (in calibration), square, straight edges, feeler gauges
Fine line and spacer blocks, or a level
Inspection sheets, release note and NCR forms
photos: The inspection plan and the item set level on supports
Camber or sweep being measured with a line or level
Twist being checked with straight edges
End plate squareness and flatness being checked
Bolt hole pitch and the bolted connection being checked
The completed inspection sheet with a release note or NCR
checklist: Planned the checks, tools and datums before measuring
Set the item level and used tools correctly
Measured camber, sweep or twist accurately
Measured hole positions from a datum and judged them against tolerance
Checked another member's readings and resolved any differences
Wrote a correct release note or NCR with a clear sketch
safety: Use lifting gear or enough people to move the item; never lift heavy steel alone
Chock the item on its supports so it cannot roll or tip
Watch for sharp edges and burrs; wear gloves
Keep walkways clear of lines and straight edges
